identification: I cannot identify 'JEV' or 'Laya' as real tools; confidence in any mapping is low (<20%). Best guess at the category, per the coordinator: Microsoft-lineage probabilistic decision tooling, i.e. MSBNx (Bayesian network editor/inference, discontinued), Infer.NET (probabilistic programming, still maintained as open source to my knowledge), and influence-diagram tools in the same family (Netica, GeNIe/SMILE, Hugin are the non-Microsoft equivalents). 'Laya' could be a mis-transcription or a name I do not know. I did not search the web, so I cannot rule out a recent tool. I earlier read 'jev' as JEPA; that reading is dropped as primary and kept only as the secondary section (I1-08, I1-09).
interpretation_note: Re-centred on Bayesian networks, influence/decision diagrams, probabilistic graphical model (PGM) inference and decision-web engines at runtime in the browser. Learned small nets are secondary. Repo facts: no eval/ directory yet (05f planned, DESIGN_NOTES.md:298-301); no model or ONNX code exists (S0); SeededRandom is a uint32 integer PRNG (src/domain/core/SeededRandom.ts:23); Psychohistory Forecast is only named in openspec/config.yaml:145; utility AI with hysteresis is planned for change 06; accepted core model has Observation table {actId|claimId, holderId, channelId, strength, confidence, learnedWatch, hops} (slices/02-systems.md). Key distinction used throughout: a PGM is a model STRUCTURE plus inference. Inference can be exact (variable elimination, junction tree) and, with fixed-point or integer arithmetic and a fixed elimination order, bit-stable. Approximate inference (sampling, MCMC, EP/variational as in Infer.NET) is the non-deterministic or heavy part. Uplift needs the structure and the exact small-network inference, not a general engine.

candidates.place: Belief/rumour inference over the Observation table (who believes what, how confident, contradictions, spoof detection)
candidates.technique: Small Bayesian-style belief update: noisy-OR/noisy-AND combination of Observations per Claim, trust-weighted by channel reliability and source Regard; per-claim naive-Bayes or tiny factor graph with <=6 parents; hop/latency decay. Not a general BN engine.
candidates.benefit: High and visible: notebook confidence that actually moves with corroboration (Obra Dinn style S2-12), rumours that distort or die, rival spoofs that fool some observers and not others, 'who else knows' derived rather than authored. Fits P4 inference trails.
candidates.determinism: Exact inference on tiny local factors is closed-form. Use integer fixed-point (0..1000 or 0..65535) with noisy-OR as 1 - product(1 - p_i) done in integers and a sorted-by-id fold order; no exp/log. Bit-stable across machines and replay-safe. Float is also stable in practice if only + * and fixed order, but integers remove doubt.
candidates.cost: Per claim per watch: O(observations on that claim). Trivial CPU. Real bound is the StateSliceStore deep clone (slice 3), not inference.
candidates.training: None. Parameters (channel reliability, decay, trust weights) are blueprint data; tune offline via 05f rollouts.
candidates.testability: Excellent in 05f: monotonicity (more independent corroboration never lowers belief), no belief without a causal path, spoof signature handling, evidence-coverage eval (RA4). Property tests on the combiner in unit tests.
candidates.fit: Pure domain reducer plus a pack-registered profile; this is core model #3 and RA3 closed-form diffusion made probabilistic. No port needed.
candidates.simpler_alternative: Scalar confidence with max/decay (no combination rule). Loses corroboration, contradiction and independence of sources, which are exactly what the notebook wants; noisy-OR is the cheapest step up.
candidates.why: The one place a probabilistic-network idea earns its keep. Implement as a fixed-point combiner on the Observation table, not as an embedded BN engine. Decide the combination rule before the Observation schema freezes (step 5 of the intro order).

candidates.place: NPC decisions: Tier-1 schemers and rivals choosing under uncertainty (influence diagram / expected-utility)
candidates.technique: Decision-theoretic selection: choose the action maximising expected utility where outcome probabilities come from the NPC's own beliefs (Observations they hold), i.e. an influence diagram evaluated by one-step lookahead, layered under the hysteresis utility AI as a scoring term. Optional: Dempster-Shafer-free simple 'subjective probability of success' per action.
candidates.benefit: Medium-high where it matters: a schemer who acts on what he believes, so false rumours and spoofs actually cause misbehaviour the player can trace back (P4). A rival who strikes because it believes it was discovered. Behaviour becomes explainable ('he believed X from channel Y').
candidates.determinism: One-step expected utility over <=10 actions and <=4 outcomes each is a few integer multiply-adds; fixed candidate order sorted by id; ties broken by SeededRandom draws in a fixed sequence. Bit-stable.
candidates.cost: Microseconds per decision per NPC. Evaluate only on deliberation boundaries (Cognitive phases already gate this) and for Tier 1/rivals only.
candidates.training: None. Utilities and outcome models are blueprint data (drives, pillars). Tune offline.
candidates.testability: 05f suite for change 06: 'NPC with false belief acts on it', 'revised belief revises behaviour without thrashing' (hysteresis), 'respects Inertia Pillars'. Golden fixtures are straightforward.
candidates.fit: Inside change 06 BehaviorModule scoring: consideration terms read the holder's Observations. Domain-pure. Keeps S2-02 motiveTag provenance (the motive is the top utility term).
candidates.simpler_alternative: Plain utility curves ignoring beliefs (reads ground truth). Cheaper but the NPC is omniscient, which defeats the whole Observation model.
candidates.why: Not a new engine: add 'consideration reads holder beliefs, with expected-utility over a tiny outcome table' to the 06 design so NPCs are not omniscient. Full influence-diagram solvers (multi-stage, optimal policies) are rejected; one-step lookahead is enough.

candidates.place: Ship Mind Psychohistory Forecast and statistical briefings
candidates.technique: (a) Closed-form hazard per thread from stage, pillar support and inertia, banded to qualitative odds; (b) Monte Carlo rollouts of the real sim from the Mind's belief-state projection; (c) a Bayesian network over thread outcomes with CPTs filled from 05f self-play frequencies (a learned-by-counting model, exact inference by enumeration).
candidates.benefit: Medium-high, thematically strong. The Mind should be wrong in explainable ways because it sees only what the Observation table lets it see. (c) gives readable causal explanations ('Synod holds the debt, so ...') which suit advisor prose.
candidates.determinism: (a) and (c): exact enumeration on a small network is closed-form and integer-able; CPTs stored as quantized integer tables in the content pack. (b): exactly deterministic if forked with a seed and the same reducers. In all cases the shown briefing is frozen into the save, so replay does not recompute it.
candidates.cost: (a)/(c): negligible. (b): N x horizon headless watch steps; no measurement exists and I did not benchmark; run in a worker at watch-spend moments. structuredClone cost (slice 3) could dominate.
candidates.training: (c) CPTs come from counting outcomes over headless self-play with the 05f runner: unlimited data, offline, deterministic, output committed as data. Needs regeneration whenever sim rules change, so wire it as an npm script and a staleness eval (CPT hash vs rules hash).
candidates.testability: Calibration eval in 05f: predicted band vs actual frequency on held-out seeds; information-hiding eval: forecast must not read facts absent from the Mind's Observations.
candidates.fit: Application port ForecastPort; pure domain inference code if (a)/(c); a worker adapter for (b). Reads a belief-state projection, never ground truth.
candidates.simpler_alternative: (a) alone. Likely 90% of the value for a qualitative briefing (R9 rejected numeric odds).
candidates.why: Start with (a); (c) is an attractive upgrade because the sim generates the CPTs for free and the result is explainable. (b) only if (a)/(c) prove too crude. Decide when change 09 is proposed; no schema work needed now beyond keeping thread stage, pillar support and per-observer knowledge queryable.

candidates.technique: Small authored plan libraries: HTN/GOAP or a goal-network (decision web) where each node is an Act template with preconditions on the rival's beliefs, plus expected-utility choice among applicable methods; a rival 'belief that it is discovered' drives escalation.
candidates.benefit: Medium-high: multi-step campaigns the player reconstructs from Acts and Observations, with tells (tellProfile). Rivals that respond to what they believe about the player's discovery risk instead of a global rank (S2-18).
candidates.determinism: Symbolic; sort applicable methods by id, tie-break with SeededRandom in a fixed order. Bit-stable.
candidates.cost: Negligible (a handful of rivals, one decision per watch).
candidates.training: None; authored, agent-assisted. Tune weights offline.
candidates.testability: 05f: 'aware at some point' invariant, plan validity, no impossible preconditions, escalation monotone with belief of discovery.
candidates.fit: Content-registered agenda blueprints emitting Acts through the BehaviorModule commit. Domain-pure.
candidates.simpler_alternative: Authored state machine per rival over thread stages. Adequate for the first epoch; HTN becomes worthwhile when agendas need replanning after player interference.
candidates.why: Start with a state machine that conditions transitions on the rival's own Observations (so belief drives behaviour); upgrade to HTN only if replanning demand appears.

candidates.place: Embedding a general PGM engine (Infer.NET-style probabilistic programming, junction tree, MCMC/EP) in the browser at runtime
candidates.technique: Port or wrap a general probabilistic inference library (JS-side BN libraries, WASM builds) and let content define arbitrary networks
candidates.benefit: Little beyond I1-01..I1-03; arbitrary networks tempt authors into opaque causal webs the player cannot read.
candidates.determinism: Exact junction-tree is deterministic if implemented with fixed order and integer/fixed-point; approximate methods (MCMC, EP, variational, as in Infer.NET) are not bit-stable unless the RNG is replaced by SeededRandom and all float ops are ordered. Third-party libraries rarely guarantee this. I am unsure of the state and licence of current JS Bayesian libraries and did not check.
candidates.cost: Exact inference is exponential in treewidth; a content-authored network can blow the 16.6 ms budget silently. Library bundle size and RAM on a 2019 i7 unknown.
candidates.training: Structure authored; parameters by counting or EM offline.
candidates.testability: Harder: every new network needs its own treewidth and runtime guard in 05f.
candidates.fit: Would need an infrastructure adapter and breaks 'domain is pure TypeScript' unless reimplemented in domain. Large dependency for small gain.
candidates.simpler_alternative: Hand-coded noisy-OR combiners and enumeration over <=8 binary variables in domain, with a hard cap on parents enforced by a contract test.
candidates.why: The structures Uplift needs are tiny and fixed; a general engine adds nondeterminism risk, bundle/RAM cost and authoring opacity. Borrow the ideas (noisy-OR, influence diagram, expected utility), not the engine.

candidates.place: Inferring player intent/style for the storyteller
candidates.technique: Counters/EMA on the Act ring (verb histogram, risk appetite, pace) driving the seeded card deck (RB3). A tiny Bayesian archetype posterior (cautious/reckless/social) from those counters is optional.
candidates.benefit: Medium: adaptive pacing, RimWorld/Left 4 Dead director style.
candidates.determinism: Integer counters and fixed-point posterior are bit-stable and saveable.
candidates.training: Archetype likelihoods are hand-set; scripted archetype bots in 05f test it. No human play data exists to learn from.
candidates.testability: Archetype bots in 05f: cautious bot yields fewer crisis_fuse in the first N watches.
candidates.fit: Derived slice from the Act ring; storyteller reads it. No port.
candidates.why: Only as counters (optionally a hand-set fixed-point posterior), tied to the storyteller work; no learning.

candidates.technique: Deterministic lexical and grounding score (tags, register, fact-id coverage, no-repeat window, seeded tie-break); a runtime embedding or cross-encoder reranker as an option
candidates.benefit: Medium: avoids repetition and chooses lines that match the LineBrief; mostly handled by authoring metadata.
candidates.determinism: Tag scoring is exact. WASM/ONNX float inference may not be bit-identical across browsers or SIMD paths; I could not verify. Mitigate by freezing the chosen line id into the save.
candidates.cost: Small embedding model is tens of MB and tens of ms per query plausibly; unmeasured, competes with the SLM tier for RAM (same spike as S2-05).
candidates.fit: Infrastructure adapter behind TextSourcePort; HF stays out of domain/application.
candidates.simpler_alternative: Metadata scoring plus offline embedding-based dedupe of the pool at authoring time.
candidates.why: Use models offline for pool curation now; a runtime reranker only if it rides on a model already loaded for the SLM tier and tag selection visibly repeats.

candidates.place: SECONDARY: learned small nets as NPC policies or runtime forecasters
candidates.technique: Tiny MLP/RL policy for NPC choice; MLP/GBDT surrogate for the Forecast trained on 05f rollouts
candidates.benefit: Little. Opaque policies harm P4 legibility and authored character; a surrogate only saves time that closed-form or counting-based CPTs (I1-03) already save.
candidates.determinism: Float inference is stable only on a fixed engine and op order; bit-stability needs int8 weights, integer matmul and lookup-table activations. Doable but extra work.
candidates.cost: Microseconds for thousands of params; not the issue.
candidates.training: Self-play data is unlimited, but reward design for 'in character' is the whole problem; surrogate goes stale on every sim change.
candidates.testability: Worse than symbolic: failures are fixed by retraining, not by editing a number.
candidates.fit: Application port plus infrastructure adapter would work technically.
candidates.why: Symbolic belief-driven decisions give the same player-visible behaviour with inspectable causes.

candidates.technique: JEPA-style joint-embedding predictor over sim trajectories
candidates.benefit: None: JEPA addresses representation learning from high-dimensional perception; Uplift state is small and symbolic, and the sim itself is the exact world model.
candidates.cost: Training pipeline overhead, no runtime need.
candidates.fit: Adapter behind a port, no domain gain.
candidates.simpler_alternative: Rollouts of the real sim or I1-03 (c).
candidates.why: Solves a problem Uplift does not have. I am unsure of current JEPA research and did not search.

candidates.place: Offline use of learning and search: parameter tuning, CPT generation, pool dedupe, exploit hunting
candidates.technique: Counting-based parameter estimation from 05f self-play (CPTs, hazard rates), random search/CMA-ES over tuning keys, archetype bots, offline embeddings for pool dedupe
candidates.benefit: High for the developer, indirect for players: balanced loops (S2-15), calibrated forecasts, fewer repeated lines. Zero runtime, RAM or determinism exposure.
candidates.determinism: Irrelevant at runtime: results are committed data with a content hash.
candidates.training: Headless sim plus 05f is exactly the data generator.
candidates.testability: Validated by 05f suites and staleness checks (data hash vs rules hash).
candidates.fit: eval/ and tooling, outside the four layers.
candidates.why: Compile-time learning, run-time data. Make 05f suites emit metrics and rollout logs usable for fitting.

recommendation: Probabilistic decision networks have a real but narrow place in Uplift, and it is as small hand-coded structures in the domain, not as an embedded engine. Adopt now: a fixed-point noisy-OR style belief combiner on the Observation table (corroboration, contradiction, spoofs, decay), and expected-utility consideration terms inside change 06 that read the deciding NPC's own beliefs so NPCs and rivals are not omniscient and false rumours cause traceable misbehaviour, which is exactly the P4 inference trail. Both are integer arithmetic in a fixed order, so they are bit-stable and replay-safe, cost microseconds, and test cleanly in 05f. For the Ship Mind Forecast, start with a closed-form per-thread hazard banded to qualitative odds, and consider a small Bayesian network whose probability tables are counted offline from 05f self-play, stored as quantized data, hash-checked against the rules, and frozen into the save when shown; rollouts from the Mind's belief state in a worker are the fallback. Reject a general probabilistic-programming or junction-tree engine (Infer.NET style) at runtime because approximate inference is not bit-stable and exact inference cost depends on author-chosen structure, and reject learned nets and JEPA for runtime. The strongest use of learning is offline: fit tables and tuning keys from self-play and commit them as data. Two schema decisions are needed before Observation freezes: the combination rule and integer scale for confidence, and a cap on parents per claim enforced by a contract test. I could not identify what 'JEV' or 'Laya' denote; if the owner meant a specific tool, confirm before anything else here is acted on.
